Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play · Conversation, family & daily routines

fun noun

also have fun, for fun, it’s fun, was it fun?, just for fun, it was pure fun, it’s no fun if you, no fun

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.1.155: per lūdum et jocum (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 1.1.27

lūdus, lūdī m.

noun, second declension

play, sport, fun

Play and fun as against serious business: per lūdum, “for fun, as a game”. Its other everyday senses are “game” and “school” (see game, school).

Other words

  • animī causā — for fun, for amusement

    also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 4.2.27 (Lewis & Short, s.v. animus); Caes. B.G. 5.12: animī voluptātisque causā (Lewis & Short)

    “For one’s own pleasure”: something done for no purpose but enjoyment.

  • jocus, jocī m. (pl. joca) — joke, jest

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.103: ad lūdum et jocum (Lewis & Short)

    Per jocum is “for fun, in jest”, as against sēriō.

  • jūcundus, jūcunda, jūcundum — pleasant, fun

    also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 1.1.78: lūdōs jūcundissimōs (Lewis & Short)

    “It’s fun” is jūcundum est; “it was great fun”, jūcundissimum fuit.

  • hilaria, hilariae f. — merriment, glee

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Laber. in Non. 108.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 98: hilaria mera erat, it was pure fun

    (vōx rāra: Laber.)

    Lewis & Short has the word from one line of the mime-writer Laberius; lūdus or jūcundus is the everyday way.

Examples

  • amōtō quaerāmus sēria lūdō

    fun aside, let us turn to serious thingsHor. S. 1.1.27 (Lewis & Short)

  • Jūcundumne fuit? — Jūcundissimum.

    Was it fun? — Great fun.composed

  • Nōn jūcundum est, sī tū …

    It’s no fun if you …Traupman 98

See also game, play, funny, I’m having a lovely time, enjoy.
